mainTopic: When are promises only 'פטומי מילי' (sweet talk)? Also, does a lender who takes a field as security acquire it if the loan is not repaid, or is that an אסמכתא that is not binding?
overview: The amud opens at the end of אמימר's ruling: when the seller states a condition that the buyer should have made, it is only 'פטומי מילי', sweet talk with no legal force. רב אשי challenges this from a ברייתא where the buyer promises to return the field, and אמימר answers that such a buyer is always treated as speaking 'of his own accord'. Next comes a story about a dying man who gives his wife a גט. She promises to be his again if he recovers, and רב זביד rules that her promise is only comforting words. The גמרא explains why that ruling was needed: without it, we might think the husband gave the גט relying on her promise. The גמרא then returns to the משנה's loan secured by a field. רב הונא and רב נחמן argue about whether a condition added after the loan wins the whole field. After רב יהודה tears up the document in a case רב נחמן decided, רב נחמן retracts and rules that the lender acquires nothing, because אסמכתא לא קניא, as מניומי taught. The משנה, which gives the field to the lender, is explained as following רבי יוסי, who holds that אסמכתא does acquire.

steps.title: The ruling: the seller's words are just sweet talk
steps.stepSummary: אמימר's ruling ends: the seller's statement has no legal force. It is only 'פטומי מילי', words to make the buyer feel good.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is just words of enticement.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes אמימר's ruling. The seller's words are nice-sounding talk and do not legally bind anyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seller made a statement that sounds like a condition of the sale. אמימר says it is not a real condition, only talk to encourage the buyer. The rest of this section asks why that is so.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Fattening words': sweet talk with no legal force
Merely, just

phrases.english: It is merely words of enticement.
phrases.notes: Literally 'fattening words'. Think of them as words meant to sweeten the deal, not real commitments.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אמימר's ruling, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The seller's statement is only friendly talk and does not bind anyone.

steps.title: רב אשי asks for the reason behind the ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי suggests a reason: this is a condition the buyer should make, so when the seller says it, it does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to אמימר: What is the reason? Since the buyer is the one who needs to make this condition, and here the seller made it, that is why you said it is just words of enticement?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי checks the reason for אמימר's ruling. This sets up his challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proposed rule is: a condition only counts when it is made by the side who is supposed to make it. Here the seller said something that belongs to the buyer, so it is just talk. Once this rule is stated clearly, it can be tested.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
To make a condition, to stipulate
Buyer
Seller

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Ameimar:
What is the reason?
Since it is the buyer who needs to make the condition,
and here the seller is the one making it,
you said it is merely words of enticement?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְאַמֵּימָר: טַעְמָא מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the ruling in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is אמימר's reason that a condition stated by the wrong party does not count?

steps.title: Challenge from the ברייתא about the buyer's promise
steps.stepSummary: In a ברייתא, the buyer says the condition that belongs to the seller, and the sale is permitted. By אמימר's logic, that should also be just talk.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא teaches: 'When you have money, I will return it to you,' and that is permitted. There, the seller is the one who needs to make the condition. The seller did not make it, and the buyer did.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings a ברייתא where the 'wrong' side spoke, the buyer this time. He is setting up a contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the buyer promises to return the field, which is a condition the seller would want. So this matches the pattern of אמימר's case: the wrong party is speaking. The next step shows why this creates a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: A taught source; here a ברייתא
When you will have money
I will return it to you
Permitted

phrases.english: But the teaching that states:
'When you have money, I will return it to you' — it is permitted;
phrases.notes: The buyer is speaking to the seller about the field he just bought.

phrases.english: where it is the seller who needs to make the condition,

phrases.aramaic: מוֹכֵר לָא אַתְנִי וְלוֹקֵחַ קָא מַתְנֵי.
phrases.english: the seller did not make it, and the buyer is making it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the rule from step 2 against a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a condition made by the wrong party is just talk.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא has the same 'wrong party' situation. Its explanation (next step) does not depend on who is speaking.

steps.title: רבא's explanation seems to say who speaks does not matter
steps.stepSummary: רבא explained that the second case of the ברייתא is where the buyer spoke of his own accord. That implies the 'wrong party' alone would not turn a statement into mere talk.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we asked: What is the difference between the first clause and the last clause? רבא said: the last clause is where he told him of his own accord. So the reason is that he spoke of his own accord. But if he had not spoken of his own accord, we would not say it is just words of enticement.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings רבא's explanation of the ברייתא and draws an inference from it. This finishes the challenge against אמימר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said the second case is permitted only because the buyer spoke 'of his own accord'. That implies that if he had not, his words would count as a real condition, even though the wrong party said them. This goes against אמימר's rule that the wrong party's words are automatically just talk.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference?
First clause / last clause
Of his own accord, on his own initiative
But otherwise (introduces an inference)

phrases.english: And we asked: What is different about the first clause
and what is different about the last clause?
And Rava said: the last clause
is where he said it to him of his own accord.
So the reason is that he said it of his own accord;
but if he did not say it of his own accord,

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָמְרִינַן פַּטּוֹמֵי מִילֵּי בְּעָלְמָא הוּא.
phrases.english: we would not say it is merely words of enticement.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the cases: רבא's 'of his own accord' explains the ברייתא, not אמימר's case. רב אשי uses it to show that the wrong party speaking was not enough to make it mere talk.
steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמְרִינַן: מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא וּמַאי שְׁנָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge from step 3 using רבא's explanation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: From 'the reason is that he spoke of his own accord', we infer that otherwise the statement would count, even though the wrong party said it.

steps.title: אמימר: the buyer's promise is always treated as 'of his own accord'
steps.stepSummary: אמימר answers that when the buyer makes this kind of statement, it is always considered as if he said it of his own accord. So there is no real contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It was taught that he is considered like one who said it of his own accord.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר defends his ruling. He explains that רבא's 'of his own accord' is not an extra requirement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אמימר, a buyer who states the seller's condition is automatically treated as speaking 'of his own accord'. So רבא's words just describe what happens whenever the wrong party speaks. The rule that the wrong party's words are just talk still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He is considered like, treated as
It was stated

steps.whatToRemember: אמימר's rule holds: a condition stated by the side not supposed to make it is just 'פטומי מילי'. The ברייתא's 'of his own accord' is simply another way of describing that same case.

phrases.english: He said to him: He is considered like one
phrases.notes: אמימר is now answering רב אשי.

phrases.english: who said it of his own accord — that is what was stated.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: נַעֲשֶׂה כְּמַאן דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ מִדַּעְתֵּיהּ אִתְּמַר
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: 'of his own accord' describes the wrong-party case, not an extra condition.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's words meant that only spontaneous statements are mere talk, so a wrong-party statement could still be binding.
steps.terutzMaskana: A buyer stating the seller's condition is automatically treated as speaking of his own accord, so it is just talk, as אמימר ruled.

steps.title: The dying man's divorce and his wife's promise
steps.stepSummary: A dying man gives his wife a גט and sighs. She promises to be his again if he recovers. רב זביד rules that her promise is only פטומי מילי.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man on his deathbed wrote a גט for his wife, and he moaned and sighed. She said to him: 'Why are you sighing? If you recover, I am yours.' רב זביד said: These are just comforting words.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that matches אמימר's idea of 'פטומי מילי'. רב זביד rules that the wife's promise is only comforting talk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wife tells her husband she will come back to him if he lives. רב זביד says she did not really bind herself. She only said it to calm him, so it has no legal force, just like the seller's words in אמימר's case.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who is dangerously ill, on his deathbed
A bill of divorce (גט)
He moaned and sighed
Comforting, 'sweetening' words with no legal force

phrases.english: There was a certain man on his deathbed
who wrote a bill of divorce for his wife
he moaned and sighed.
She said to him: Why are you sighing?
If you recover, I am yours.
Rav Zevid said:
These are merely words of comfort.
phrases.notes: This is the same phrase אמימר used about the seller. It means sweet talk that doesn't bind anyone.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא שְׁכִיב מְרַע, דִּכְתַב לַהּ גִּיטָּא לִדְבֵיתְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel case of 'פטומי מילי' after the discussion of אמימר's ruling ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wife's promise to remarry her divorcing husband if he recovers is only comforting words and does not bind her.

steps.title: Why does רב זביד even need to say this?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא מדפתי asks רבינא why רב זביד needed to rule this. Even a real condition from the wife would mean nothing, because conditions in a גט are set by the husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא מדפתי said to רבינא: And if it were not just comforting words, so what? Is it up to her to put a condition into a גט? It is up to him to put in a condition!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא challenges whether רב זביד's ruling was needed at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband is the one who gives the גט, so only he can attach a condition to it. If so, the wife's words could never count as a condition, whether they were sweet talk or not. So רב זביד's ruling seems to teach us nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא from the town of Difti
A condition
It is in his hands, up to him
To place, put in (a condition)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha of Difti said to Ravina:
And if they were not words of comfort, what of it?
Is it up to her
to put a condition into a bill of divorce?
It is up to him to put in a condition!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether רב זביד's ruling was needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רב זביד's statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only the husband can set conditions in a גט. So the wife's words could never count, and calling them 'פטומי מילי' adds nothing.

steps.title: We might have thought he gave the גט relying on her promise
steps.stepSummary: The answer: without רב זביד, we might think the husband decided to give the גט because of her promise. Then it would be like his own condition. רב זביד teaches that it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that he himself relied on her words when he decided to give the גט. So רב זביד teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב אחא and shows why רב זביד's ruling is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: True, the wife cannot set a condition on her own. But we might have thought the husband accepted her promise and gave the גט on that basis, making it his own condition. רב זביד teaches that her words were only comfort, so the husband did not build on them, and the גט has no condition.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)
Relying on her intent or words
Decided and gave
It teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: Comforting words like 'If you recover, I am yours' bind no one. The husband is not seen as giving the גט based on them.

phrases.english: Lest you say:
he himself, relying on her words,
decided to give the bill of divorce
it teaches us otherwise.
phrases.notes: This means רב זביד's ruling teaches us that the husband did not rely on her promise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחא's challenge from step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the ruling is needed to block a mistaken assumption (מהו דתימא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The husband gave the גט relying on her promise, so it would be like his own condition.
steps.terutzMaskana: Her words were only comfort. He did not rely on them, and there is no condition.

steps.title: Loan secured by a field: when was the condition said?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's case of a loan secured by a field. רב הונא says the timing of the condition matters. רב נחמן says that even after the money was given, the lender acquires the whole field.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he lent him money on his field: רב הונא says, if the condition was said when the money was given, the lender acquires the whole field. If it was said after the money was given, he acquires only as much as his money is worth. רב נחמן says: even after the money was given, he acquires all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now quotes a new line from the משנה and brings a מחלוקת between רב הונא and רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's lender said, 'If you don't repay in three years, the field is mine.' רב הונא says this works for the whole field only if he said it when he handed over the loan. If he said it later, he gets only a share of the field matching the loan. רב נחמן says he gets the whole field either way.

keyTerms.meaning: He lent him money with his field as security
The giving of the money (the loan)
He acquired everything (the whole field)
Matching the value of his money

steps.confusionAlert: At this stage, both sides agree a condition said at the time of the loan gets the whole field. They argue only about a condition added afterward. In step 13, רב נחמן changes his mind and says even that gets nothing.

phrases.english: If he lent him money on his field,
phrases.notes: These are words from the משנה. There the lender said: if you don't repay within three years, the field is mine.

phrases.english: Rav Huna says:
At the time of giving the money, he acquired it all.
phrases.notes: This means if the lender stated his condition at that moment.

phrases.english: After the giving of the money,
he acquired only the part matching his money.
And Rav Nachman says:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ לְאַחַר מַתַּן מָעוֹת – קָנָה הַכֹּל.
phrases.english: Even after the giving of the money, he acquired it all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the next case in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא: a condition added after the loan gets only a share of the field matching the loan. רב נחמן: it gets the whole field.

steps.title: רב נחמן rules by his view, and רב יהודה tears the document
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן decided a real case in the court of the ריש גלותא according to his own view. רב יהודה tore up the document.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן decided a case at the ריש גלותא's court by his own ruling. רב יהודה tore up his document.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about רב נחמן's view being used in practice and then rejected by רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן gave the lender the whole field even though the condition was added after the loan. רב יהודה tore up the lender's document, which shows he did not accept that ruling. The next step tells how רב נחמן reacted.

keyTerms.meaning: A real case, a practical ruling
The Exilarch, head of the Jews in Bavel
According to his own ruling
A legal document, deed

phrases.english: Rav Nachman decided a case
at the Exilarch's court, according to his own ruling,
phrases.notes: His own ruling was that even a condition added later gets the lender the whole field.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda tore up his document.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רב נחמן's view from step 9 being used in a real case and then challenged.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יהודה rejected רב נחמן's ruling in practice by tearing up the document.

steps.title: רב נחמן: a great man must have had a reason
steps.stepSummary: The ריש גלותא tells רב נחמן that רב יהודה tore his document. רב נחמן answers that a great man did it, so he must have seen a good reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ריש גלותא said to him: 'רב יהודה tore up your document.' He answered: 'Did a child tear it? A great man tore it. He saw a reason in it, and tore it!'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן responds to the news that his ruling was overturned. He does not fight it, and he respects רב יהודה's decision.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן says this was not a careless act by a beginner. רב יהודה is a great scholar, so he must have found a real reason why the document was not valid. The story ends with רב נחמן giving weight to רב יהודה's judgment.

keyTerms.meaning: A child, a young beginner
A great man, a great scholar
A reason

steps.whyThisMatters: The story shows that רב נחמן himself respected רב יהודה's ruling against him. That gives weight to the view that a condition added after the loan does not win the whole field.

phrases.english: The Exilarch said to him:
Rav Yehuda tore up your document.
He said to him: Did a child tear it up?
A great man tore it up;
he saw a reason in it and tore it up!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא: רַב יְהוּדָה קְרַע לִשְׁטָרָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells how רב נחמן reacted to רב יהודה tearing the document in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The ריש גלותא's report suggests רב נחמן's ruling was overturned. How would he react?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A great scholar like רב יהודה must have seen a valid reason, so the tearing is accepted.

steps.title: A second version of רב נחמן's reply
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רב נחמן dismisses רב יהודה's tearing of the document, saying that in monetary law everyone is like a child compared to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רב נחמן answered differently: 'A child tore it up. Compared to me, everyone is a child when it comes to monetary law.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of what רב נחמן told the ריש גלותא after רב יהודה tore up his document. In this version, he does not respect the tearing at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version (step 11), רב נחמן assumed רב יהודה had a good reason. Here רב נחמן stands by his own ruling, because he sees himself as the top expert in monetary law. So the two versions disagree about whether רב נחמן accepted the challenge or brushed it off.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who say: introduces a second version of the same story or teaching
A small child
Law; here, monetary law

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new event. It is the same reply from step 11, just told a different way.

phrases.english: There are those who say: he said to him:
phrases.notes: 'He' is רב נחמן, answering the ריש גלותא from the last step.

phrases.english: A child tore it up,
for everyone, compared to me,
in monetary law, are children.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of רב נחמן's answer from step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב נחמן dismisses רב יהודה's act, because he considers himself the greater expert in monetary law.

steps.title: רב נחמן changes his ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן retracts. He now holds that even if the condition was stated when the money was given, the lender acquires nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Later רב נחמן said: Even if the condition was made at the time the money was given, the lender acquires nothing at all.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן takes back his earlier view and gives a new ruling on the field case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9, רב נחמן said that even when the condition came after the money was given, the lender gets the whole field. Now he goes to the opposite extreme: even when the condition was made at the time of the loan, the lender gets nothing. So timing no longer matters at all. The condition simply does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: Went back; here, he changed his mind
The giving of the money (when the loan is handed over)
He acquired nothing at all

steps.whyThisMatters: This retraction sets up the whole discussion that follows about why such a condition fails.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman then went back and said:
Even at the time the money is given,
he has not acquired anything at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the story of the torn document, רב נחמן reverses his own earlier ruling from step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A condition that the field becomes the lender's if the loan is not repaid does not work at all, even if it was made when the money was given.

steps.title: רבא challenges רב נחמן from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes the משנה, which says that if the borrower does not pay within three years, the field belongs to the lender.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected to רב נחמן from the משנה: 'If you do not pay me within three years, the field is mine.' And the משנה rules that it is his!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב נחמן's new ruling by quoting our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה clearly says the condition works and the field goes to the lender. That goes directly against רב נחמן's new ruling that the lender acquires nothing. So how can רב נחמן argue with a משנה?

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him (usually from a משנה or ברייתא)
It is his (the field belongs to the lender)

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection to Rav Nachman:
If you do not give me the money
from now until three years,
it is mine,
phrases.notes: These are the lender's words in the משנה. 'It' is the field.

phrases.english: it is his!
phrases.notes: This is the משנה's ruling: the field goes to the lender.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the new ruling of step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that the lender acquires nothing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה explicitly rules that the field becomes the lender's, which contradicts רב נחמן.

steps.title: רב נחמן explains: מניומי taught that אסמכתא does not acquire
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says he used to hold that an אסמכתא works, but מניומי said it does not, and he now follows מניומי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I used to say that an אסמכתא acquires. But מניומי said that an אסמכתא does not acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן explains why he changed his mind. The condition in the משנה is an אסמכתא, and he now agrees with מניומי that an אסמכתא does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אסמכתא is a promise a person makes because he is confident it will never come into effect. Here the borrower is sure he will pay on time. Since he never truly meant to give up the field, the deal is not binding. רב נחמן's earlier view matched the משנה, but מניומי convinced him otherwise.

keyTerms.meaning: A conditional promise made without full intent, because the person expects the condition never to happen
Acquires; is binding
A sage whose view רב נחמן accepted

steps.confusionAlert: 'אני אומר' here means 'I used to say', not 'I say now'. רב נחמן is describing his old view.

phrases.english: He said to him: I used to say
that an asmachta acquires.
But Minyumi said:
an asmachta does not acquire.
phrases.notes: He means: I was convinced by מניומי, so I changed my ruling.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנִי אוֹמֵר אַסְמַכְתָּא קָנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge by explaining the reason for the retraction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Admits that the משנה fits his old view, and explains that he changed his view based on מניומי.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אסמכתא is binding, so the lender gets the field, as the משנה says.
steps.terutzMaskana: אסמכתא is not binding, so the lender gets nothing.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule אסמכתא לא קניא is a major principle in monetary law across ש״ס.

steps.title: The משנה is difficult for מניומי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how מניומי can hold that אסמכתא does not acquire, when the משנה says the field goes to the lender.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to מניומי, the משנה is a difficulty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short, sharp question on מניומי's view, using the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן only explained why he changed his mind. That does not solve the main problem: the משנה itself says an אסמכתא works. So מניומי's view still seems to go against a משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a difficulty
Our משנה

phrases.english: But according to Minyumi, the mishna is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the challenge from step 14, now aimed directly at מניומי.
steps.kashyaTarget: מניומי's rule that אסמכתא לא קניא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה rules that the field goes to the lender, which means an אסמכתא does acquire.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי יוסי, who holds that אסמכתא acquires. מניומי does not follow that view.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: our משנה follows רבי יוסי, who said that an אסמכתא acquires.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question on מניומי. The משנה follows the opinion of one תנא, רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a disagreement among the תנאים about whether an אסמכתא works. The משנה follows רבי יוסי, who holds it does. מניומי follows the other side, so the משנה is no problem for him.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say: introduces a possible answer
A תנא who holds that אסמכתא acquires

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן retracted and now holds אסמכתא לא קניא, following מניומי. Our משנה, which lets the lender take the field, follows רבי יוסי, who holds אסמכתא קניא.

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
the mishna is according to Rabbi Yosei,
who said that an asmachta acquires.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא מַתְנִיתִין רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הִיא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the משנה to one תנא (רבי יוסי) whose view מניומי does not follow.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is the accepted ruling, so אסמכתא acquires.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows only רבי יוסי, so מניומי may hold otherwise.
